South Texas record early voting hints at a Valley shift this election cycle, experts say
 Share: 
By: Armando Gomez 
Related Story
 McAllen, TX (KRGV) — Rio Grande Valley voters headed to the polls on Election Day after early voting reached record turnout compared to previous midterm elections.
 Outside the Lark Community Center in McAllen, a line of voters stretched out the door. Voters there said this midterm election is consequential.
 "I think it is important to have our voices be heard, especially in this midterm election, and it is very important for the state of Texas," Amy Soto said.
 Other voters emphasized the importance of exercising their right to vote.
 "Basically, have your voice heard. It's a great way to have it out there, and I honestly don't take it for granted being able to vote every two years when you have the opportunity to express your opinion or express your choices, so I think it is a great opportunity," Will Ramirez said.
 Channel 5 News spoke with a political science professor about what is driving voters to the polls. Experts say the races on the ballot are one factor behind the record turnout.
 "There are a lot of reasons to vote against the current administration and the current party in power, and I think for Republican-leaning voters it's the desire to make sure the Democrats don't get into office," South Texas College political science instructor Kevin Holton said.
 Holton said the high turnout could also signal a shift in voting patterns.
 "What I also think it means is that we may see the Valley tilt back toward Democrats in this current cycle. In 2024 there was a shift toward the right, we might see some of the voters coming home," Holton said.
 Early voting results will not be released until the last person in line has voted. Stay tuned for full-team Election Day coverage, and click here for Election Day resources and unofficial results.
